title: HIGH PERFORMANCE INSULATING MATERIALS FOR L4 ENCELADUS LANDER - EXPRO+
description: To assess the potential use of alternative insulating materials (e.g. aerogel) to improve the thermal performance of classical MLI,and sustaining the extreme environments applicable to L4 Enceladus Lander.Current thermal insulation solutions for Solar System missions are mainly based onconductive and radiative insulation (e.g. JUICE Nomex reinforced MLI), or includeconvective insulation function, not assessed for L4 Enceladus Lander environments (e.g.ExoMars Upilex foam). Due to the L4 Lander extreme environment on Enceladus (lowtemperatures, potential interaction with plumes, snow and/or ice and challenging landingconditions), the use of classical MLI technology, even with an efficient, reinforced designsuch as the one used in JUICE, is probably insufficient to achieve the required thermalinsulation and reduce the use of electrical heating. Heaters use is to be minimized (with atarget of 0 W), as the electrical power consumption is directly linked to the mass andlifetime span of the Lander on Enceladus surface. In addition, the selected thermal controltechnologies shall ensure nominal performance while keeping physical integrity (stringentmechanical loads during landing) and fulfilling mass, EMC, planetary protection and otherrequirements of the mission.Potential technologies such as Aerogel have been identified in similar missions such asMars Pathfinder ("(...). The WEB is a thermal isolating composite structure with cocuredthermal control surfaces and an ultralightweight hydrophobic solid silica aerogel whichminimizes conduction and radiation. This design provides excellent thermal insulation atlow gas pressures and meets the structural requirements for spacecraftlaunch loads andfor a 60 g impact landing at Mars without damage to the insulation or structure. (...)",https://www.jstor.org/stable/44725574). The use of these technologies or alternative onesneeds being assessed for L4 Enceladus Lander. The activity encompasses the followingtasks:Requirements consolidation and assessment of state of the art- Design of breadboard and associated test bench- Manufacture of breadboard, test bench- Execution of tests and exploitation of results- Conclusions elaboration and roadmap for further development towards a flight applicationThe outcomes of this activity are extendable to other planetary missions.
